milestone.title: Approval integrity — full-spec drafts, a real approve gate, and needs_regrooming on post-approval spec edits

intent.outcome: A milestone is authored whole in draft (ACs, work packages, steps) and becomes approved only through `mp milestone approve`, which checks the spec is executable. After approval, any material spec edit flags the milestone (needs_regrooming), is recorded in the activity journal, shows up in mp validate and in raul, and blocks the start of execution until it is re-approved.

problem.description: Approval currently means very little. (1) Nothing gates entry: milestone/spec.rs::approve_milestone is just apply_spec_status(ctx, id, "ready"), identical to `mp milestone set-spec-status <id> ready`, so a bare draft with no steps becomes lifecycle approved in one call (observed creating M247). (2) Decomposition is ordered backwards: wp.rs:26 and step.rs:28 refuse work packages / steps below spec_status ready, so the fragment commands only work after approval, and `mp milestone create --json` rejects work_packages and steps: CreateMilestoneInput has both fields (spec.rs ~112-114, applied ~463-470) but the CREATE_MILESTONE_KEYS allow-list (spec.rs ~190) omits them — so a full spec cannot be authored in draft at all. (3) Nothing notices changes after approval: on 2026-09-27, 16 approved milestones were materially rewritten (titles, scope, ACs, steps) with no signal; needs_regrooming stayed false. The model already has MilestoneEvent::SetNeedsRegrooming and the needs_regrooming overlay (mp-model milestone.rs ~451, ~584), and raul's milestone detail renders it (render/milestone_detail.rs ~45, ~238), but no CLI path ever sets it. Harm is both execution (a runner or autopilot executes ACs the approver never saw) and audit (no record of what changed after approval).

in_scope: Draft decomposition: add work_packages and steps to CREATE_MILESTONE_KEYS so `mp milestone create --json` accepts a full spec; WP and step authoring commands (add / update / split / remove) work in draft; execution writers (step claim / set-status / done / fail) still require an approved milestone. `mp milestone create --example` shows work_packages and steps.

Approve gate in approve_milestone (first approval and re-approval): at least one WP; every AC has a verification and is covered by a step; every step covers an existing AC and belongs to an existing WP; depends_on_steps reference existing steps with no cycle; `mp interview gaps` clean. Failure: non-zero exit with a structured list of violations; `--dry-run` reports the gate result without writing.
Breaking: `mp milestone set-spec-status <id> ready` fails with a hint to run `mp milestone approve <id>`; other spec statuses behave as before.

Approval baseline: at approve time store an optional `approval` block in milestone meta (approved_at + one hash per material field). Material fields: intent, problem, scope, depends_on, acceptance_criteria (id, description, verification), work_packages (id, name, goal), steps (id, action, files, tests, done_when, covers_ac, depends_on_steps, work_package). Not material: statuses, evidence, claims, priority, effort, risk, comments, notes, design decisions, flow stages.

Detection in the single milestone write path (milestone/io.rs::write_milestone_synced; route any direct store::write_milestone callers for milestones through it): when the milestone is approved and every step is pending, compare material hashes with the baseline; on mismatch dispatch SetNeedsRegrooming(true) and append a `spec-revised` activity event listing the changed fields. A milestone with no baseline gets one on its first save, with no flag.

Re-approval: `mp milestone approve <id>` on a flagged milestone re-runs the gate, clears the flag, refreshes the baseline, and appends `spec-reapproved` with the fields changed since the previous approval.
mp validate emits a new warning for every milestone with needs_regrooming true; mp path shows a re-approve action for it.

Execution gate: while needs_regrooming is true, step claim / set-status (in-progress, done) / done refuse without --force, and `mp autopilot start` refuses to queue the milestone without --force; each --force use appends a `force-bypassed` activity event.
raul: `mp list milestones` rows carry needs_regrooming (additive; regenerate the json-shape golden); raul's Milestones rows and Path items show a `revised` chip in palette.warn when it is true.

Rollout: replace `set-spec-status … ready` with `mp milestone approve` across crates/mp/tests, tests/ (golden scenarios and fixtures), templates/skills, docs, and scripts; document the approve gate and the revision flow in docs/milestones/ and docs/mp/commands.md; CHANGELOG entry marked breaking.
out_of_scope: Milestones already in execution (any step not pending): edits are not flagged.
Blocking or refusing spec edits — grooming stays unblocked.
Storing full approved snapshots or a diff-since-approval command (hashes + changed-field lists only).
Backfilling flags for milestones rewritten before this ships (first save records the baseline).
Approving from raul (raul only displays the flag).
A deprecation period for set-spec-status ready.

acceptance_criteria.description: In draft, WP and step add / update / split / remove succeed; step claim / set-status / done / fail are refused until the milestone is approved.
mp milestone create --json with ACs, WPs, and steps produces a complete draft (lifecycle draft); --example includes work_packages and steps.

mp milestone approve rejects each gate violation (no WP, AC without verification, uncovered AC, step without AC, step without WP, unknown or cyclic step dependency, interview gaps) with a structured reason, approves a complete spec, and --dry-run reports the gate result without writing.
mp milestone set-spec-status <id> ready fails with a hint naming mp milestone approve; other spec statuses are unchanged.

On an approved, not-started milestone, a material edit sets needs_regrooming and appends spec-revised listing the changed fields; non-material edits (priority, comment, design decision, status, evidence) do not; a milestone without a baseline gets one on first save without being flagged.
While flagged, mp validate warns and mp path offers re-approval; mp milestone approve re-runs the gate, clears the flag, refreshes the baseline, and appends spec-reapproved.
While flagged, step claim / set-status / done are refused without --force and mp autopilot start refuses the milestone without --force; each --force use appends force-bypassed.
acceptance_criteria.verification: cargo nextest run -p mp --no-fail-fast --test approval_integrity -E 'test(/execution_gate/)' && cargo nextest run -p mp --no-fail-fast --test autopilot_drive_preconditions -E 'test(/needs_regrooming/)'

acceptance_criteria.description: mp list milestones rows carry needs_regrooming (json-shape golden regenerated additively) and raul's Milestones rows and Path items show a `revised` chip when it is true.
acceptance_criteria.verification: cargo nextest run -p mp --test suite_misc --no-fail-fast -E 'test(/^json_shape_baseline::/)' && cargo nextest run -p raul --no-fail-fast -E 'test(/revised_chip/)'

acceptance_criteria.description: No test, scenario, fixture, skill template, doc, or script relies on set-spec-status … ready to approve (the rejection test excepted); golden scenarios pass; docs describe the approve gate and revision flow.
acceptance_criteria.verification: ! rg -q 'set-spec-status \S+ ready' crates/mp/tests tests templates docs scripts --glob '!approval_integrity.rs' && make test-scenarios && rg -q 'needs_regrooming' docs/milestones

acceptance_criteria.description: mp and raul tests, clippy, fmt, and consumer-surface lint are clean.
acceptance_criteria.verification: cargo nextest run -p mp -p raul --no-fail-fast && cargo clippy -p mp -p raul --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --all -- --check && make consumer-surface-lint

design_decisions.choice: Milestones are authored whole in draft: intent, problem, scope, ACs, work packages and steps. Approval is the single explicit gate between a full spec and execution.
design_decisions.rationale: Decomposition gated on approval forces approval of half-specs (set-spec-status ready is the only way to unlock WP/step writers), which defeats the purpose of review.

design_decisions.choice: mp milestone approve runs the full readiness check (interview gaps clean, every AC covered by a step, no weak verifications, refs resolve) and records an approve event; set-spec-status ready no longer implies approval (breaking change shipped now).
design_decisions.rationale: A gate that can be bypassed by a status flip is not a gate; consumers are few enough that a clean break is cheaper than a deprecation window.

design_decisions.choice: Detect material spec edits centrally in the milestone save path by comparing a spec fingerprint against the baseline recorded at approval; the baseline is created on first save after this ships, with no backfill of historical approvals. Material = intent, problem, scope, ACs, WPs, steps (not notes, status or metadata).
design_decisions.rationale: A central hook catches every writer (fragment commands, update --json, bulk) without per-command wiring; skipping backfill avoids guessing what historical approvals covered.

design_decisions.choice: A material edit after approval sets needs_regrooming and blocks execution writers (step claim / done, autopilot drive) until mp milestone approve re-approves; --force bypasses and is journaled as recorded debt.
design_decisions.rationale: Flag-and-gate keeps edits cheap while making unreviewed scope changes visible and non-executable; --force matches the repo's existing debt semantics.

design_decisions.choice: raul shows a 'revised' chip on milestones with needs_regrooming in this milestone; milestones already in flight at ship time are out of scope (no retroactive flagging).
design_decisions.rationale: The human reviewer needs to see the flag where they review; retro-flagging in-flight work would stall current execution for no new information.
